Projet : Projet de Développement des Chaines de Valeur Vivrières (PDC2V)

No Crédit: Crédit IDA N°69080

             

Intitulé du Marché : Acquisition d'équipements supplémentaires nécessaires pour l'accréditation du LANADA

Emis le :  21 Octobre 2025

 

  1. La République de Côte d’Ivoire a reçu un crédit de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement pour financer le Projet de Développement des Chaines de Valeur Vivrières (PDC2V), et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché relatif à l’acquisition d'équipements supplémentaires nécessaires pour l'accréditation du LANADA.
  2. L’Unité de Coordination du PDC2V sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir les équipements techniques nécessaires à l’accréditation du LANADA.
  3. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence nationale telle que définie dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale de septembre 2025, et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.
  4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’Unité de Coordination du PDC2V aux adresses suivantes : (Voir Mme KOUABENAN SOLOU Edwige, Spécialiste en Passation des marchés) ; edwige.solou@pdc2v.ci avec copie à patrick.kramo@pdc2v.ci et examiner le Dossier d’Appel à cotations ou prendre connaissance du dossier à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous de 8 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 17 heures, Temps Universel.
  5. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir gratuitement un dossier de demande de cotations en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.
  6. Les cotations devront être soumises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le jeudi 5 novembre 2025 à 10 heures précises temps universel. Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project

Indicative Activity / Budget Line

Component 2: Enabling Environment and Regulatory Harmonization - Payment System Oversight and Regulation.

Activity Reference Number (STEP)

FJ-PIFS-577115-CS-INDV

Assignment Title

Payments System Advisor to the Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF)

Location of role

Suva, Fiji, with remote inputs. The balance of on-site and remote support will be agreed with RBF and PIFS against the implementation schedule.

Implementing Agency on behalf of participating countries

Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS)

Primary Counterpart

Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF)

Duration of Assignment

Approximately six (6) months for the core assignment. Limited follow-up support for participant onboarding may be agreed through 30 June 2027.

Contract Type and Level of Effort

Time-based individual consultant contract. The expected level of effort is up to 120 working days over 6 months. Payments will be based on approved timesheets and eligible reimbursable expenses, rather than fixed-price deliverables.

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum brings the region together to address shared issues and support cooperation. It works through regional governance, shared resources and policy alignment to support economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security.

Selection Method

Competitive Selection of an independent individual consultant, subject to procurement plan adjustment, justification, conflict-of-interest review, and World Bank no-objection requirements where applicable.

Country Supported

Fiji. The assignment provides country-specific technical assistance under the regional CBR Project.

Overall Project Objective

To enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries.

Project Length

August 2024 to September 30, 2030

Project Background

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) for the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships (CBR) Project. The project supports participating Pacific Island Countries to maintain access to correspondent banking services and address payment, regulatory and financial integrity constraints that contribute to de-risking. Component 2 includes support for payment system oversight and regulation.

The Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF) issued the Fiji QR Code Standard and Guidelines to the payments industry on 30 October 2025. RBF has also issued a directive and implementation timeline requiring payment service providers that currently offer QR payment services, or intends to introduce them, to align with the prescribed standards and guidelines by 30 June 2027.

RBF’s planned implementation includes a cloud-based solution to act as the QR payments Certificate Authority (CA) for participating payment service providers, to be operated by RBF. At the time of its August 2026 feedback, RBF expected the vendor to be appointed by the end of that month, followed by approximately three months of development and implementation. RBF will confirm the procurement status and implementation timetable before the assignment commences.

The CA vendor is responsible for the platform-specific technical work and documentation included in its contract. RBF has requested technical assistance at the overall QR project level, covering implementation leadership, project management guidance, technical advisory support, quality assurance, participant integration, user testing, project documentation and training. The assignment will also support RBF in addressing National Payment System (NPS) configuration requirements for accepting QR payments.

 

Objective of the Assignment

The objective is to support RBF in leading, coordinating and assuring the implementation and operational readiness of the Fiji QR Code Standardisation Project. The consultant will provide project-wide implementation support and technical advice so that participating institutions, payment-system arrangements and operating procedures are prepared for QR payments in line with the Fiji QR Code Standard and Guidelines.

The consultant will work under RBF’s direction and help coordinate the contributions of vendors, participating institutions and RBF teams. RBF will retain responsibility for project decisions and approvals, including approval of system changes and production launch.

 

Scope of Services

The consultant will work with RBF, participating financial institutions and payment service providers, the CA vendor, other relevant technical providers, PIFS and the World Bank. The following six areas cover the overall QR project. Detailed activities and sequencing will be agreed in the inception work plan.

i. Implementation planning governance and coordination

Support RBF in leading the overall QR implementation and coordinating the work of participating institutions and relevant vendors. Review the applicable standards, guidelines and project plans, and prepare a coordinated work plan covering system preparation, participant integration, testing, training and launch. Provide project management guidance, maintain the project schedule and action tracker, and help RBF address risks, dependencies, reporting protocols, and decisions that affect delivery.

ii. Technical review and implementation support

Provide technical advice and project-level quality assurance across the QR payment process, including participant connectivity, interoperability, payment processing, security, resilience and operational responsibilities.   Support RBF in identifying, reviewing and coordinating the NPS configuration changes required to accept QR payments.  Review proposed changes and implementation evidence with the responsible technical teams, and track issues requiring resolution. Review CA-related interfaces and dependencies where these affect the wider QR project and support RBF review CA/PKI operating framework, including certificate renewal, revocation, key rollovers and overall certificate lifecycle management, without duplicating the vendor’s contracted technical work.

iii. Participant integration and testing

Support participant integration planning and coordinate a common approach to integration testing and user acceptance testing. Prepare or consolidate project-level test plans, test cases and readiness criteria; coordinate test activities; review results; and track issues through correction and retesting. Testing should cover QR code generation and validation, interoperability between participants, payment processing through the relevant NPS arrangements, security and recovery. CA-related tests will be coordinated with the vendor’s testing programme.

iv. Operational procedures and project documentation

Prepare or consolidate the procedures, templates and working documents needed to manage the QR project and support scheme operations. These should cover project governance, participant onboarding, testing, risk and issue tracking, operational responsibilities, incident handling, reporting and launch readiness. Review relevant vendor and participant documentation for consistency with the overall implementation plan. Platform-specific manuals and other CA documentation required under the vendor contract will remain the vendor’s responsibility.

v. Capacity building

Provide practical training and knowledge transfer to RBF staff and participating institutions on QR project implementation, participant responsibilities, testing, operational procedures, incident handling, stakeholder engagement, communications, awareness, adoption activities and ongoing oversight. Include project management guidance for the RBF team and practical use of the documents and templates prepared under the assignment. Coordinate training with vendor-provided instruction so that system-specific training and project-wide capacity building complement each other.

vi. Readiness and implementation support

Support RBF in assessing readiness for pilot testing,  and production launch across the QR project, including participant readiness, completion of user testing, NPS configuration, operating procedures and support arrangements. Identify outstanding issues, recommend actions and help coordinate the initial implementation period. Prepare a completion and handover report with remaining actions and arrangements for continued participant onboarding through the industry compliance deadline.

 

Vii. Clearing, settlement, reconciliation, operations and service management  

Provide support in defining transaction routing, clearing and settlement arrangements, liquidity and finality considerations, reconciliation, exception handling, failed transaction, reversals, refunds and dispute handling procedures. Assist RBF develop managment reports covering transaction volume and value, avilability, failure, fraud, complaints, merchant coverage and adoption, Develop dashboards, data standards and compliance monitoring.   

Scope Exclusions

The consultant will provide independent advisory, coordination and quality assurance support. The CA vendor will remain responsible for developing, configuring, documenting and correcting the CA solution and for other outputs required by its contract. Participating institutions and the responsible system operators or technical providers will remain responsible for implementing changes to their own systems, including authorised NPS configuration changes.

This TOR does not assign the consultant responsibility for software development, production-system administration or delivery of the CA vendor’s contractual obligations. Any independent cybersecurity testing or technical audit will require a separately agreed scope and confirmation of the procurement arrangements before commissioning.

Expected Outputs and Reporting Obligations

The consultant will prepare the following working products in line with the agreed implementation schedule. The inception work plan will confirm submission dates, review responsibilities and dependencies on RBF, vendors and participating institutions. The outputs cover the overall QR project and should incorporate or refer to vendor documentation where appropriate.

Expected Output

Content

Indicative Timing

1. Inception Report and Work Plan

Confirmed QR project scope, implementation plan, roles and responsibilities, schedule, dependencies, initial risk register and coordination arrangements.

At inception

2. Technical and Integration Review

Project-level technical review and advice on participant integration, NPS configuration for QR payments, implementation issues, quality assurance and recommended actions.

During implementation; updated as required

3. Testing and Participant Readiness Package

Integration and user acceptance test plans and cases, readiness criteria, issue tracker and summary of test results and corrective actions.

 

Before and during testing

4. Operational Documentation and Training Package

QR project and operating procedures, templates, working guidance, training materials and records of capacity-building activities.

Before launch and handover

5. Implementation Readiness and Completion Report

Readiness assessment before launch; completion and handover record at the end of the core assignment, including outstanding actions and continued participant onboarding.

Before the launch decision and at assignment completion

 

Reporting Obligations

The consultant will report administratively to the Project Coordinator within the PIFS Project Management Unit (PMU) and work with RBF on a day-to-day technical basis. Technical priorities, work planning and expected outputs will be agreed with RBF, PIFS and the World Bank project team. Coordination will include the PIFS Payment Systems Specialist and Fiji Country Coordinator as relevant.

Short monthly activity notes will summarise work undertaken, meetings held, outputs prepared, implementation progress, issues requiring decisions and planned activities. The consultant will maintain a current action tracker covering responsibilities, deadlines, risks and dependencies, and provide additional progress updates during testing and launch preparation as agreed with RBF. Timesheets and payment documentation will be provided as required by the agreed contract.

Technical outputs will be submitted to RBF and PIFS for review and shared with the World Bank where required under project arrangements. The consultant will incorporate consolidated comments and provide final working products in editable formats, together with a completion and handover record.

Monthly progress update report to be provided to RBF by the 5th working day of the new month.

 

Duration, Location and Institutional Arrangements

The core assignment is expected to run for approximately six months, aligned with the overall QR implementation plan and the CA vendor’s implementation timetable. A limited amount of follow-up support may be required for additional participant onboarding before 30 June 2027. The level of effort and any follow-up period will be agreed before contracting, subject to project needs and available budget.

The assignment will combine work in Suva and remote support. The consultant will propose an input schedule that supports implementation coordination, participant testing, training and launch preparation. The number and identity of initial participants and the balance of on-site and remote inputs will be confirmed with RBF and PIFS.

PIFS will contract the consultant through the Pacific Strengthening CBR Project. RBF will act as the primary technical counterpart, designate the relevant staff and facilitate engagement with the CA vendor, participating institutions and other technical providers. RBF will provide access to relevant standards, guidelines, project documentation and technical information, subject to confidentiality requirements. Meeting facilities and workspace may be provided subject to availability.

 

Performance Indicators

Performance will be assessed through the quality and timeliness of the agreed outputs and the consultant’s support to RBF. The assessment will consider whether the implementation plan and action tracker are maintained; technical and NPS configuration issues are documented and escalated; participant testing and readiness are supported by evidence; and procedures, training and handover materials are usable by RBF after the assignment.

The consultant’s performance will be assessed against its agreed responsibilities. Vendor delivery, participant system changes and RBF approval decisions will remain with the responsible parties, with the consultant expected to identify dependencies and report delays or unresolved issues promptly.

 

Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

The consultant shall comply with PIFS and applicable World Bank requirements on confidentiality, conflicts of interest, anti-corruption and prevention of fraudulent practices. Sensitive RBF, vendor and participant information shall be used only for the assignment and shall not be published or disclosed without prior written consent from PIFS and RBF, and World Bank clearance where required.

The consultant shall disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest before contract signature and throughout the assignment, including relationships with the CA vendor or participating institutions. The consultant must be able to provide independent advice and quality assurance and shall not review its own vendor deliverables. Participation in related downstream procurement shall be subject to applicable conflict-of-interest restrictions.

 

Consultant Qualification Requirements

The assignment requires a consultant or consulting team with experience in payment systems implementation and the ability to coordinate a multi-participant QR project. The lead consultant or Team Leader should meet the experience requirement below, with access to specialist inputs appropriate to the agreed scope.

Area

Qualification / Experience

Lead consultant / Team Leader

At least 10 years of relevant experience in payment systems or digital payments, including prior support to a central bank, payment system operator or financial-sector regulator.

Project management and coordination

Experience leading or coordinating payment-system implementation, managing vendor and participant dependencies, and providing project management guidance and implementation advice.

QR payments and system integration

Experience with QR code payment schemes, interoperability, payment processing and participant integration, including the payment-system configuration requirements for QR payments.

Quality assurance and testing

Experience with system integration testing, user acceptance testing, production readiness, cybersecurity and operational resilience for payment systems.

Documentation and capacity building

Ability to prepare payment-system procedures, technical and project documentation, templates and training materials, and deliver practical capacity building for RBF and participating institutions.

Specialist inputs

Access to payment-system configuration, cybersecurity and testing expertise, and to public key infrastructure (PKI) / Certificate Authority expertise where needed to address QR integration dependencies. These inputs must respect the CA vendor’s contractual responsibilities.

Regional experience

Experience in Fiji, the Pacific or other small and capacity-constrained markets would be an advantage.

 

Selection Method

The selection process will follow the approved procurement plan and applicable PIFS and World Bank requirements. The procurement documents will specify the evaluation approach for the confirmed consulting arrangement and the requirements set out above. The contract will confirm fees, input schedule, travel arrangements, reporting obligations and confidentiality and conflict-of-interest undertakings.

REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO

Agence pour le Développement et la Promotion du Projet Grand Inga
(ADPI-RDC)

Programme de Développement du Projet Inga 3 « PDI3 »

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

(SELECTION DE CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL)

 

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT ASSUMANT LA FONCTION DE SPECIALISTE EN PASSATION DES MARCHES AU SEIN DE L'AGENCE POUR LE DEVELOPPEMENT ET LA PROMOTION DU PROJET GRAND INGA (ADPI-RDC) DANS LE CADRE DU PROGRAMME DE DEVELOPPEMENT INGA 3 (PDI3)

 

N° de crédit / N° de don : 7816-ZR (A) & 7815-ZR (B)

N° de référence de l’Avis : ZR-ADEPI-570694-CS-INDV

Date de Publication : le 21 octobre 2026

Date de clôture : le 04 novembre 2026

 

1. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de sa stratégie de réduction du déficit énergétique au niveau national, le Gouvernement de la RDC a demandé et obtenu de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) deux lignes de crédit (A et B) pour financer le « Programme de Développement du Projet INGA 3 (PDI 3) », et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie de ce crédit en vue d’effectuer des paiements au titre d’un contrat pour les prestations des services d’un(e) « Consultant assumant la fonction de deuxième Spécialiste en Passation des marchés au sein de l'Agence pour le Développement et la Promotion du Projet Grand Inga (ADPI-RDC) dans le cadre du Programme de Développement Inga 3 (PDI3)».

 

2. Au titre des services, sous l’autorité du Directeur Général d’ADPI-RDC en attendant l’arrivée du Directeur de Projet du PDI3 et sous la supervision du Responsable de l’unité de la Passation des Marchés du PDI3, le deuxième Spécialiste en Passation de Marchés est chargé d'apporter son appui à la mise en œuvre des activités de passation des marchés du PDI3 conformément au Règlement de passation de marchés de la Banque Mondiale et d’éventuels autres bailleurs de fonds.

 

De manière spécifique, le (la) Consultant(e) aura comme responsabilité, entre autres de :

  • Élaborer, mettre à jour et assurer le suivi du Plan de passation des marchés (PPM) ainsi que des calendriers des procédures, conformément au PTBA, aux accords de financement et aux procédures de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Préparer les dossiers de passation des marchés, notamment les DAO, les demandes de propositions, les avis à manifestation d’intérêt et les lettres d’invitation, et veiller à leur approbation ainsi qu’à l’obtention des avis de non-objection requis ;
  • Appuyer la conduite des procédures de passation des marchés, participer aux séances d’ouverture des plis et aux travaux des commissions d’évaluation et des marchés, et assurer le contrôle qualité des rapports d’évaluation ;
  • Préparer les contrats et veiller à leur approbation, signature, notification et suivi dans les délais requis ;
  • Assurer le suivi de l’exécution des marchés et des contrats, notamment le respect des obligations contractuelles, des délais, des spécifications techniques et des exigences de qualité ;
  • Veiller à la bonne tenue, à la conservation et à l’archivage des dossiers de passation des marchés, ainsi qu’à la mise à jour des outils de suivi et à la préparation des rapports périodiques ;
  • Contribuer à l’élaboration et à l’actualisation des manuels de procédures, au traitement des réclamations des soumissionnaires et à la résolution des difficultés liées à l’exécution des contrats ;
  • Participer aux missions de supervision du projet, au renforcement des capacités des acteurs impliqués et au transfert de compétences en matière de passation des marchés ;
  • Veiller au respect des dispositions des accords de financement et des procédures de passation des marchés applicables aux acquisitions de travaux, de fournitures et de services ;
  • Exécuter toute autre tâche relevant de ses compétences et nécessaire à la bonne mise en œuvre des activités du projet.

 

3. La durée de la mission est de douze (12) mois, renouvelable sous réserve d’une évaluation satisfaisante des performances du Consultant.

 

Le temps de prestation est fixé à un minimum de quarante (40) heures par semaine, à raison d’au moins huit (8) heures par jour, sur le lieu de travail ou en dehors de celui-ci, selon les nécessités de la mission et les dispositions contractuelles applicables.

 

Le Consultant exercera ses fonctions au sein de l’ADPI-RDC, à Kinshasa, République démocratique du Congo.

 

4. L’Agence pour le Développement et la Promotion du Projet Grand Inga (ADPI-RDC) invite les candidats (Consultants Individuels) admissibles à manifester leur intérêt pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter de cette mission.

 

5. Le/la Consultant(e) à recruter devra disposer des qualifications et expériences requises ci-après :

  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 ou équivalent en économie, finance, droit, sciences commerciales, ingénierie ou dans un domaine pertinent ;
  • Justifier d’une formation complémentaire en passation des marchés suivant les procédures de partenaires financiers multilatéraux ou bilatéraux ;
  • Justifier d’au moins dix (10) années d’expérience professionnelle générale en passation des marchés ;
  • Justifier d’au moins huit (8) années d’expérience en qualité de spécialiste de la passation des marchés publics dans des projets de développement financés par la Banque mondiale ou la Banque africaine de développement, l’expérience dans un projet financé par la Banque mondiale constituant un atout ;
  • Justifier d’au moins deux (2) années d’expérience dans des projets ou programmes d’infrastructures comportant des contrats de complexité et/ou de valeur importante, financés par des partenaires techniques et financiers au cours des dix (10) dernières années ;
  • Avoir conduit avec succès des opérations de passation des marchés dans au moins deux (2) grands projets d’infrastructures au cours des dix (10) dernières années, dont au moins un projet d’un montant supérieur ou égal à cent millions de dollars américains (100 000 000 USD) ;
  • Avoir une parfaite maîtrise du français, à l’écrit comme à l’oral ;
  • Maîtriser les logiciels bureautiques courants, notamment Microsoft Word, Excel et PowerPoint ;
  • Maîtriser les règles et procédures de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale et de la Banque africaine de développement, ainsi que les dispositions pertinentes des accords de financement ;
  • Une expérience en passation des marchés suivant les procédures communautaires constituera un atout.

 

NB : Le candidat doit citer les principaux/gros contrats signés dans le cadre des projets sur lesquels il a intervenu en qualité de de spécialiste en passation de marché, ainsi que la méthode de passation de marché et le  le montant du contrat.

 

Le dossier de candidature devra inclure :

  • Une lettre de motivation signée et datée
  • Un curriculum vitae signé et daté renseignant entre autres les expériences passées et les informations sur les personnes de référence
  • Les copies des diplômes académiques
  • Les attestations de travail antérieur.

 

6. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projet d’investissement (FPI) », édition révisée de septembre 2025 ci-après désigné « Règlement de Passation des Marchés », qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables.

Implementation Plan for Renewable Energy, Energy Efficiency and E-Mobility under the
Energy Act, 2025 and National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding Petroleum Provisions –

REGAIN Project

Project ID: P181250
Assignment Type: International Firm (Lump sum Contract)
Duration: 9 Months
Location: Remote with Periodic Missions to Majuro
1. Background
The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is one of the world's smallest and most isolated nations. The
country consists of 29 atolls and 5 low coral islands situated on about 181 square kilometers (km 2 ) of land mass
in the Pacific Ocean. Majuro (the nation's capital) and Ebeye, the country's two largest urban centers, account
for about 96 percent of the total population, while the remaining inhabitants live on the outer atolls. The
Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) depends mostly on diesel generation to meet the
country's growing electricity needs. The country aims to enhance its energy security through renewable energy
generation, improve the reliability of electricity supply, enhance energy efficiency, expand e-mobility, and
improve access to electricity. Increased energy resilience will reduce dependence on hydrocarbon fuels, insulate
the country from the risks of price rises and supply uncertainties, and equip it with natural disaster-resilient
electricity infrastructure.
MEC, the state-owned energy utility, generates and provides electricity to Majuro Atoll, serving 55 percent of
RMI's population. MEC also manages three mini-grids in Jaluit, Wotje, Rongrong (Majuro Atoll), and Kili
Island, the latter having been recently transferred to MEC from the Kili Bikini Ejit (KBE) Local Government.
Following the integration of the Kwajalein Atoll Joint Utilities Resources (KAJUR) into MEC, MEC is also
responsible for power generation and distribution in Ebeye, together with the water and sewerage services
previously provided by KAJUR. MEC is responsible for executing plans to enhance energy security but lacks
the capability to conceive and implement them. It lacks the funds required to implement these plans. The
Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has partnered with the World Bank through the
Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase Project (REGAIN) – an IDA grant of US$60 million
approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030. The REGAIN
project aims to increase renewable energy generation and improve access to electricity while reducing reliance
on diesel-based generation through funding and technical support.
RMI’s Electricity Roadmap targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and 100% renewable electricity by 2050.
As a small and geographically dispersed island nation, RMI remains highly dependent on imported diesel for
electricity generation, exposing the country to high energy costs and vulnerability to global fuel price shocks
and supply disruptions. To manage this risk, RMI needs to diversify its electricity supply portfolio by

6
integrating more RE, manage demand growth by promoting efficient electricity use, pursue new business
opportunities such as EVs, and monitor and report implementation status to the GRMI for appropriate course
correction. Ensuring a reliable, clean, and cost-effective electricity supply is therefore critical to achieving
national climate commitments, strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable socio-economic
development. The country lacks the legal, policy, and regulatory framework, institutional capability, and the
trained manpower required to achieve these objectives. The GRMI has taken some steps in this direction, such
as the notification of the Energy Act 2025, which provides a legal, policy, regulatory, and organizational
framework to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply for the benefit of RMI’s
economy and citizens and to promote the efficient use of energy and of energy from indigenous sources.
Under Sub-Component 3.1 of the REGAIN project (Sector Development Assistance), MEC plans to seek
consultancy support from a firm to propose a roadmap and undertake proposed activities for the Implementation
of the Energy Act (IEA) 2025. In the roadmap, IEA shall propose activities to be undertaken in the short,
medium, and long term and undertake them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by
focusing on regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course
correction to promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply in RMI.
IEA shall be prepared in close coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and
MEC.
IEA shall take into account all Acts, policies, regulations, studies and current practices relevant to electricity (all
RE included), Energy Efficiency, E-mobility and their funding, including but not limited to:
Energy Act 2025
National Energy Authority Act, 2025
Recommendations contained in Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan 2024-2034
Electricity Roadmap of 2018, which provides a relevant and guiding framework for the sector’s
development
MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model, prepared by MEC’s Supplemental Management and
Operations (SMO) consultant under ADB-funded technical assistance, which covers MEC’s operations
prior to the integration of KAJUR and on which the tariff review under Task 6 shall build
National Targets and the progress achieved against them to date
Relevant energy sector programs and studies of other development partners active in the RMI, in
particular the Asian Development Bank (ADB), such as the Energy Transition Project, should be taken
into account to ensure coordination and avoid duplication.
The assignment will support GRMI, MEC, and NEA in translating the Energy Act, 2025, and the National
Energy Authority Act, 2025, into an actionable implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency,
and e-mobility. The assignment will identify required policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-
building actions, while excluding provisions related to the petroleum sector. This support aligns with REGAIN’s
institutional strengthening objectives and RMI’s need to reduce reliance on diesel, improve energy security, and
support the integration of renewable energy.

7
2. Objectives
The objective of the assignment is to prepare a practical, time-bound implementation plan for renewable energy,
energy efficiency, and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025,
excluding petroleum-sector provisions, and to support the preparation of priority policy, regulatory, institutional,
monitoring, and capacity-building instruments required for implementation.

Institutional strengthening for the implementation of RE, EE, and e-mobility provisions.
Policy and regulatory framework, guidelines for the development of higher RE integration, EE
promotion, and e-mobility uptake.
Monitoring and reporting framework for RE, EE, and e-mobility targets, progress, and
implementation gaps.
Database/reporting arrangements for RE, EE, and e-mobility information.
Capacity development strategy for institutions, utilities, and local manpower.

3. Project Description
This assignment is financed by the World Bank under the institutional strengthening and implementation
support activities of REGAIN. It will support the policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, and capacity-
building measures required to implement the RE, EE, and E-mobility provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and
the National Energy Authority Act, 2025.
4. Implementation Arrangements
MEC will be the Employer and the contracting authority for this assignment, responsible for approving
deliverables and payments. The Consultant may proceed to the next deliverable under MEC's general guidance.
NEA, as the statutory authority responsible for regulating the energy sector, shall be responsible for the
technical and regulatory approval of policy- and regulation-driven deliverables. MEC, as Employer, retains
ultimate authority for administrative and financial approval and for the release of REGAIN project funds, which
shall follow NEA's technical sign-off on the relevant deliverable. The responsible ministry and Cabinet shall be
consulted where recommendations require policy approval, regulatory adoption, statutory action, budget
allocation, or cross-government implementation. MEC shall be responsible for formal approval of all
deliverables and payments. The Consultant shall work under the direction of MEC and coordinate closely with:

MEC management and technical staff
REGAIN Project Management Services Consultant, as applicable
Project Implementation Unit (PMU) within MEC
NEA, the national regulatory body, serving as the regulatory interface between MEC and the
Consultant
Responsible Ministry and Cabinet on policy formulation
World Bank on matters requiring no-objection, reporting, or implementation support
ADB and other development partners active in RMI's energy sector, as relevant

Petroleum-sector implementation matters are excluded from this assignment.

8
5. Scope of Services
The scope of services is limited to the electricity sector, in particular renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-
mobility, including relevant non-petroleum legal, policy, regulatory, institutional, monitoring, enforcement,
data, and capacity-building provisions necessary for their implementation. Petroleum sector related provisions
of the Energy Act, 2025, are excluded from the assignment. While MEC is the Contracting Employer for the
entire assignment, NEA serves as the primary technical Client for Tasks 1, 2, 3, and 7, given their statutory and
regulatory content. MEC's approval of these deliverables is administrative and financial and follows NEA's
technical acceptance.
Task 1: Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall
Islands
The Consultant shall review and map the existing institutional arrangement, policy, and regulatory framework
against the provisions and the directions contained in the Energy Act (EA) 2025 and the National Energy
Authority (NEA) Act 2025 (harmonious reading) for the development of Renewable Energy (RE), Energy
Efficiency (EE), and E-Mobility (E-MB). The Consultant will propose a strategy to address misaligned or
missing institutional arrangements, policies, and regulatory framework.
(i) Review of existing applicable policies, strategies, plans, and studies in the context of the requirements
of EA 2025 and NEA Act 2025,
(ii) Identify whether the gap is institutional, policy, or regulatory, whether it will be addressed within the
existing framework (alignment/modification), or whether a new framework is to be created, and
(iii) Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and Institutional framework to address these gaps.
Task 2: Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector related international and national
commitments and targets
The Consultant will undertake a focused review of the GRMI's international commitments, national targets,
initiatives for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, and the progress achieved. The diagnostic and strategic
review will include the following:
(i) Discussion with the stakeholders and ascertaining reasons for the shortfall in the envisaged progress,
(ii) The Consultant shall review relevant national targets, international commitments, ongoing initiatives,
and selected comparable Pacific/SIDS practices for RE, EE, and e-mobility implementation. The
purpose of the review shall be to identify practical options for policy, regulatory, institutional,
monitoring, and capacity-building measures suitable for RMI,
(iii) Identification of implementation gaps, in particular critical legal, policy, regulatory, and institutional
gaps, which impacted the achievements of these initiatives and targets,
(iv) Assess whether these legal, policy, and regulatory gaps stem from implementation shortfall or a missing
framework, and
(v) Recommend a broad policy, regulatory, and institutional framework to address these gaps.
Task 3: Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps
The Consultant will propose a strategy with a time-bound implementation roadmap for addressing the gaps
identified in Tasks 1 and 2. The proposed strategy will include the following:
(i) Identification of Implementation gaps, i.e., the framework/provision exists but has not been
implemented, or there is a shortfall in its implementation,
(ii) Identification of gaps in the existing framework, i.e., the legal, policy, regulatory, or Institutional
framework provides for the enabling provision, but it has not been enacted or notified; indicate whether
it is a policy, regulatory, or institutional issue,

9
(iii) Identify misalignment (even a section or provision of it) of the policy, regulatory framework, or the
institutional framework with the EA 2025 and NEA 2025,
(iv) Identification of gaps that cannot be dealt with by the existing framework,
(v) Recommendation of a strategy to deal with these identified gaps. The proposed strategy will indicate the
required interventions (legal, policy, regulatory and institutional), their implementation order, the
stakeholders responsible for addressing them and the timelines within which these will be addressed
(short term- within 3 months, medium term- within 6 months and long term-within 12 months) duly
aligned with the statutory timelines provided in the Acts and related policies,
(vi) Indicate how the recommended interventions will address the identified gaps.
(vii) Indicate the way forward for the gaps which cannot be addressed under the existing legal framework,
and
(viii) Develop a comprehensive implementation roadmap considering the recommendations made in Task 2
and in this Task, and compile the recommendations.
The roadmap should indicate:
Short-term actions,
Medium-term actions,
Long-term actions,
Responsible institution,
Required decision or instrument,
Dependency,
Level of priority, and
Whether the consultant will draft the instrument under this assignment.
Task 4: Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the sector
The Consultant will examine whether the current institutional structure, including its roles and responsibilities,
aligns with those prescribed in the Energy Act and is conducive to the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in
RMI. The Consultant will examine the following:
(i) Clarity in their role and responsibilities (without any overlap) for the development of RE, EE, and E-
MB,
(ii) The institutional capacity to lead the development of RE, EE, and E-MB in RMI, such as project
planning, design, implementation, operation, and maintenance, and
(iii) Recommendations for addressing institutional alignment of roles and responsibilities, capacity gaps, and
the coordination mechanism between them for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB, taking into
account the integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC.
The Consultant will also assess the skills and the manpower required for the development of RE, EE, and E-MB
in RMI. The Consultant shall assess:
(i) Manpower and the skills available with all important stakeholders,
(ii) Assess the manpower and the skill requirements considering the national targets and the evolving
(proposed Roadmap) legal, policy, regulatory and institutional framework for the development of RE,
EE and E-MB for the next 5 years,
(iii) Indicate the gaps between availability and requirements, and
(iv) Prepare a strategy to meet this gap, indicating the number, the skill requirements, and how the required
skills will be met (contents of the training, how and where the training will be provided, suggestions for
international collaboration, certification).

10
Task 5: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE
The Consultant will assess the status of the RE database to determine its suitability for publishing a report that
records, documents, and shares critical information on RE, EE, and E-MB. The Consultant will:
(i) Evaluate the existing database and identify the missing indicators/information gap/data field necessary
for various stakeholders to discharge their roles and responsibilities for the development of RE, EE, and
E-MB in the country (covering Majuro, Ebeye and the outer island systems),
(ii) Recommend formats, information to be gathered, sources of this information, reporting institutions,
reporting frequency, and validation process,
(iii) Recommend the structure of the report to be published, and
(iv) Prepare the first RE encompassing the above recommendations, which NEA can subsequently update
and improve upon.
Task 6: Electricity tariff review and recommendations
The tariff review shall build on, and not duplicate, MEC’s current tariff methodology and tariff model prepared
by the SMO consultant. It shall focus on how that methodology has performed in practice, on areas it did not
examine in depth, and on extending it to all systems now operated by MEC, including Ebeye following the
integration of KAJUR’s operations into MEC, which was not covered by the earlier work. The review shall also
provide MEC and NEA with a clear, evidence-based rationale and supporting calculations for the recommended
tariff options, so that they are well prepared to respond to tariff proposals from policymakers, investors and
other stakeholders.
The Consultant shall review the existing electricity tariff arrangements and prepare recommendations and an
implementation pathway that are consistent with the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act,
2025. The Consultant shall, in particular:
(i) Assess the adequacy of the current tariff level, structure, adjustment mechanisms, billing arrangements
and related subsidy or compensation mechanisms;
(ii) Assess the revenue requirement and efficient cost of electricity service, based on verified utility
financial, operational and investment data;
(iii) Determine the extent to which prevailing tariffs and practices align with the principles contemplated
under the relevant sections of the Energy Act;
(iv) Assess tariff implications of planned renewable energy, EE, E-mobility, battery storage, network,
resilience and access investments;
(v) Recommend refinements to the existing tariff methodology, tariff structure, adjustment mechanism and
regulatory review process that NEA can use in tariff determinations;
(vi) Review the application of MEC’s current tariff methodology and identify any issues, anomalies or
unintended outcomes that have emerged in practice and that may require adjustment;
(vii) Extend the revenue-requirement and cost-of-supply analysis to Ebeye following the integration of
KAJUR’s operations into MEC, including harmonization of KAJUR’s financial, operational and
customer data with MEC’s, clear separation of electricity costs from water and sewerage costs, and
options and a transition pathway for bringing Ebeye’s electricity tariff into MEC’s tariff framework;
(viii) Assess the merits and implications of the planned introduction of a single tariff for all customer classes;
(ix) Assess whether a uniform national tariff should be maintained across all MEC-served systems (Majuro,
Ebeye and the outer islands), or whether location-specific tariffs or tariff adjustment factors are
warranted, including the resulting cross-subsidies between locations;

11
(x) Using the known sizes and costs of the hybrid and mini-grid systems to be installed in the outer islands,
estimate the indicative cost of supply and potential tariff for each location, and assess the implications of
any proposal to reduce tariffs in locations with high renewable energy penetration;
(xi) Assess the practicality, timing and customer impact of reducing or removing existing government
subsidies, and the alternatives available;
(xii) Assess the feasibility of time-of-use tariffs that reflect the different costs of daytime (predominantly
solar) and nighttime (predominantly diesel) supply;
(xiii) Recommend tariffs and charging arrangements for electric vehicle charging;
(xiv) Assess feed-in tariff, net-metering and power purchase arrangements for privately owned renewable
energy systems seeking to export to MEC’s grid, including pricing based on avoided cost, the grid
integration, storage and backup costs borne by MEC, and the volume of such generation the grid can
accommodate;
(xv) Assess the implications of electricity supplied by third parties outside MEC’s networks, such as
renewable energy systems at government or private facilities that supply neighboring communities,
including the pricing basis and regulatory requirements for such supply, and how differences between
their prices and cost-reflective MEC tariffs can be explained and managed;
(xvi) Assess distributional and affordability implications for customer classes, including vulnerable
customers, and identify transparent options for any subsidy or compensation that may be required; and
(xvii) Provide practical inputs for preparation and future implementation of the National Electricity Tariff and
Billing Code.
Task 7: Addressing the recommendations
Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap under Task 3, and working under the
technical supervision of NEA, the Consultant shall identify, prepare, revise or align the policies, regulations,
codes, guidelines and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act,
2025 and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions.
The Consultant shall, in particular:
(i) Prepare or align the electricity-sector regulatory instruments identified as necessary under the Acts,
including, as applicable, electricity licensing, electricity-sector regulation, Grid Code, service standards,
universal service and subsidy-related mechanisms,
(ii) Prepare or align the instruments required for renewable energy, including, as applicable, grid integration,
renewable IPPs, community renewable-energy projects, rooftop installations and renewable microgrids,
(iii) Prepare or align the instruments required for energy efficiency, including applicable standards, labeling
requirements, air-conditioning and cooling energy-efficiency requirements, and other EE measures
required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts,
(iv) Prepare or align the instruments required for e-mobility, including applicable requirements relating to
charging infrastructure, technical standards, charging services, electricity supply and tariff arrangements,
and other matters required to implement the applicable provisions of the Acts, and
(v) Propose the institutional framework and clearly define the roles and responsibilities of the relevant
institutions for implementation.

7. Fees and Reimbursable Expenses
As this engagement will be structured as a lump-sum contract, the selected Consultant shall submit a financial
proposal (in addition to a technical proposal) that includes:
A total lump-sum price for the performance of the services, payable against the deliverables set
out in Section VIII, supported by a breakdown of professional fees by each proposed expert and
personnel category, indicating the applicable unit rates and estimated level of effort (person-months
or person-days), provided for information purposes; and

14
Reimbursable expenses, included within the lump-sum price, covering any anticipated travel,
accommodation, per diem, logistics, communications, and other project-related costs necessary for
the performance of the services.

The lump-sum price shall be inclusive of all costs necessary for the performance of the services. The Consultant
shall clearly state the assumptions underlying the proposed costs and provide sufficient detail to allow MEC to
assess the reasonableness of the proposed budget.
8. Deliverables
The project has six (6) main deliverables.
The Consultant shall prepare and submit the following deliverables in accordance with the Scope of Services.
The Task references identify the principal Tasks contributing to each deliverable and shall not limit the
Consultant's obligation to take into account relevant findings and recommendations arising from other Tasks.
1. Deliverable 1: Inception Report (Linked to: Tasks 1 to 7)
The Consultant shall submit an Inception Report confirming its understanding of the assignment, methodology,
work plan, stakeholder engagement arrangements, data and information requirements, and detailed schedule for
carrying out the seven Tasks and submitting the required deliverables.
An Inception Workshop shall be conducted with MEC, NEA, and other relevant stakeholders, and agreed
outcomes shall be reflected in the final Inception Report.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within two weeks of Notice to Proceed (NTP).
2. Deliverable 2: Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap (Linked to: Tasks 1, 2 and 3)
The Consultant shall prepare a consolidated Diagnostic Assessment and Implementation Roadmap for the
relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, relating to
renewable energy, energy efficiency, and e-mobility.
The deliverable shall consolidate the diagnostic and strategic reviews, identify and categorize the principal
implementation, policy, regulatory, and institutional gaps and misalignments, and establish a prioritized, time-
bound roadmap to address them.
The roadmap shall identify responsible institutions, required actions, sequencing, dependencies, priorities, and
the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines to be prepared or aligned under this assignment.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within ten weeks of the NTP.
3. Deliverable 3: Institutional and Capacity Development Framework (Linked to: Task 4 and relevant
institutional findings from Tasks 1 to 3)
The Consultant shall prepare an Institutional and Capacity Development Framework setting out the
recommended institutional arrangements, roles and responsibilities, coordination arrangements, manpower and
skills requirements, identified capacity gaps, and capacity-development strategy for RE, EE and e-mobility.

15
The proposed framework shall be consistent with the findings and priorities established under Deliverable 2
The Deliverable shall be submitted within eighteen weeks of the NTP.
4. Deliverable 4: Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework and RE Report (Linked to: Task 5)
The Consultant shall prepare the Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for monitoring progress in
RE, EE and e-mobility, including the recommended database, data collection, validation and reporting
arrangements and institutional responsibilities.
The deliverable shall include the recommended database and reporting arrangements and the first RE Report,
prepared in a form suitable for subsequent updating by NEA.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-four weeks of the NTP.
5. Deliverable 5: Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations (Linked to: Task 6)
The Consultant shall prepare a stand-alone Electricity Tariff Review and Recommendations Report, presenting
the assessment, findings, and recommended tariff and regulatory pathway in accordance with Task 6.
The deliverable shall provide the analytical and regulatory basis necessary to support tariff-related decisions and the
preparation or implementation of the applicable tariff and billing regulatory framework.
The deliverable shall also include the updated tariff model in editable form, covering all MEC-served systems
including Ebeye, and concise briefing notes setting out the rationale and supporting calculations for the
recommended tariff positions, for use by MEC and NEA in policy and stakeholder discussions.
The Deliverable shall be submitted within twenty-six weeks of the NTP.
6. Deliverable 6: Policies, Regulations, Codes and Guidelines for Implementation of the Energy Act
(Linked to: Task 7, informed by Tasks 1, 2 and 3)
Based on the approved recommendations and implementation roadmap, the Consultant shall prepare and/or
align the policies, regulations, codes, and guidelines identified as necessary to implement the relevant
provisions of the Energy Act, 2025, and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, within the scope of the
assignment.
The deliverable shall comprise the agreed package of new and/or revised policies, regulations, codes and
guidelines covering, as applicable:
Electricity-sector regulation;
Renewable energy;
Energy efficiency, including air-conditioning and cooling; and
E-mobility.
The policies, regulations, codes and guidelines shall be consistent with the gaps, priorities and sequencing
established through the preceding Tasks and agreed with NEA and MEC.

16
The Deliverable shall be submitted within thirty-two weeks of the NTP.
9. Contract Duration
The contract duration is 9 months. The expected start date is January 2027.
10. Evaluation Criteria
The Consultant will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications-Based Selection (CQS) method in
accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and the REGAIN Procurement
Plan. Interested firms shall submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) demonstrating their qualifications and
relevant experience. EOIs will be evaluated against the criteria below. The most qualified and experienced firm
will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal and, if responsive, to negotiate a contract.
Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans
for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points)
Experience in electricity tariff, cost-of-service and revenue-requirement studies for small island or multi-
system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points)
Experience in the Pacific or other Small Island Developing States (25 points)
Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including core business, years in business, organization
and availability of relevant expertise (15 points)
Total: 100 points
Key experts will not be evaluated at the EOI stage. The qualifications of the proposed key experts set out in
Section 6 will be reviewed when the selected firm submits its technical proposal.
11. Inputs to be provided by MEC and NEA
MEC, as the Employer, and NEA, as the technical and regulatory counterpart, shall provide or facilitate timely
access to the information, documents, data, personnel, and stakeholders reasonably required for the performance
of the Services, to the extent available.
NEA shall:

sector targets, reports, databases and other relevant regulatory information,
Provide available information on institutional arrangements, regulatory processes, staffing and capacity
relevant to the assignment,
Facilitate access to relevant officials and stakeholders for consultations and workshops, and
Review and provide timely technical comments and acceptance of deliverables submitted to it for review
or acceptance.
MEC shall:
Provide or facilitate access to relevant technical, operational, customer, commercial, financial and
investment information and data, including information required for the tariff review, covering all MEC-
served systems including Ebeye (former KAJUR operations), and MEC’s current tariff methodology and
tariff model,

17
Provide available plans, studies, reports, databases and information relating to existing and planned RE,
EE, e-mobility, storage, and network,
Facilitate access to relevant MEC and PMU personnel and stakeholder consultations, and
Undertake the contractual, administrative and financial review and approval of deliverables in
accordance with the implementation arrangements.
The Consultant shall, as part of the Inception Report, submit a consolidated data and information request
specifying the information required, its proposed source, format and required date. The Consultant shall
promptly identify material data gaps and propose appropriate alternative sources, assumptions or methodologies
where required.
The provision of information by MEC, NEA or any other stakeholder shall not relieve the Consultant of its
responsibility for the verification, analysis, adequacy and quality of the Services and deliverables required under
the Contract.

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to Prepare a National Land Use Plan for Belize.

The Government of Belize has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the Belize Blue Cities and Beyond Project and intends to apply part of the Project’s proceeds to contract a firm to prepare a National Land Use Plan for Belize.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve the preparation of a comprehensive and legally sound National Land Use Plan (NLU Plan) for Belize. The assignment will operationalize the National Land Use Policy (NLUP) by establishing a national spatial and technical framework to guide sustainable land use, zoning, and development across sectors and administrative levels. The consultancy will include situational analysis, preparation of strategic and zoning frameworks, stakeholder consultations, development of digital and GIS-enabled planning tools, institutional strengthening, capacity building, and establishment of a monitoring and evaluation framework.

The assignment will be implemented under the Belize Blue Cities and Beyond Project, managed by the Central Executing Unit (CEU) within the Ministry of Finance, in collaboration with the Ministry of Natural Resources, Petroleum and Mining, through the Lands and Surveys Department.

Implementation Period:

The duration of the consultancy is eighteen (18) months.

Expected Start Date:

The consultancy is expected to commence following completion of the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) process and contract signing. Based on the application submission deadline of October 30, 2026, at 9:00 AM, the anticipated start date is the beginning of 2027.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest and can be found at the following website: https://procurement.gov.bz/mof-ceu-consultancy-services-to-prepare-a-national-land-use-plan-for-belize-ceu-firm-bz-ceu-460793-cs-qcbs-mof-ceu-2026/

Interested Firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:  

  1. General Experience: Demonstrated experience in national or regional land use planning, spatial planning, or sustainable land management assignments for public sector institutions, including the preparation of policy, regulatory, or strategic planning instruments. Firms should have completed at least two (2) similar assignments of comparable scope and complexity.
  2. Specific Experience: The Firm must demonstrate experience in at least two (2) similar assignments within the last ten (10) years involving the preparation of national or regional land use plans, spatial development frameworks, or zoning instruments. Experience in integrating spatial analysis, stakeholder consultations, and institutional capacity support will be considered an asset.
  3. Adequacy of Assignment: At least two (2) references must be submitted and should demonstrate assignments of comparable scope and institutional context, involving coordination with government entities, preparation of comprehensive planning instruments, and support to implementation or institutional strengthening processes.

The shortlist will contain not fewer than five (5) and not more than eight (8) eligible firms.

L’objectif général de la mission est de réaliser un diagnostic élargi des 30 Centres d’Enseignement des Métiers (CEM) appuyés par le PACEJ, afin d’analyser les filières existantes et identifier les filières prioritaires à développer ou à renforcer, les besoins en ressources humaines et les référentiels de formation nécessaires à leur mise en œuvre et à l’utilisation efficiente des équipements fournis par le Projet, ainsi que les mesures à proposer pour améliorer l’attractivité, la pertinence et l’efficacité de la formation par alternance dans les CEM.   • Expérience générale dans le domaine de la formation technique et professionnelle ou de l’apprentissage ;
  • Expérience spécifique dans la réalisation de diagnostics, d’études de terrain ou d’analyses des besoins en compétences (au moins 3 missions) ;
  • Connaissance du contexte national, des CEM et des enjeux d’insertion professionnelle des jeunes ;
  • Qualité des livrables antérieurs et capacité de rédaction en français.
  • Disponibilité pour réaliser la mission dans le délai d’un mois.

Il/elle veille à l’intégration de la nutrition dans la conception et la mise en œuvre des interventions agricoles et de sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle du Projet, et contribue à l’amélioration de la diversité et des pratiques alimentaires des ménages bénéficiaires.

  • Une spécialisation en nutrition publique, en agriculture sensible à la nutrition ou agriculture climato-résiliente serait un atout
  • Justifier d’au moins dix (10) années d’expériences professionnelles pertinentes dont au moins deux (2) années en qualité de spécialiste ou dans une fonction de responsabilité technique comparable au sein des projets/programmes de développement rural financés par des bailleurs de fonds nationaux et/ou internationaux ;

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Individual Consultant Selection

Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS)

Reference No.: ET-ESS-574164-CS-INDV

Hiring of Social Safeguards Specialist

The Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) intends to recruit a Social Safeguards Specialist under the Modernizing Ethiopia's Statistical System Project (MESSP) Preparation Grant, financed by the World Bank.

The Social Safeguards Specialist will support the implementation of social risk management, stakeholder engagement, grievance redress, labour management, inclusion, and SEA/SH prevention activities under MESSP in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable national laws. The position will help ensure that social risks are proactively identified, monitored, reported, and addressed, and that project activities are implemented in a manner that is inclusive, transparent, and consistent with the project's social commitments.

Duty Station: ESS Headquarters, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Reporting: The Social Safeguards Specialist will report to the Project Manager.

Contract Duration: Full-time assignment. The contract shall commence upon recruitment and cover the project preparation phase and subsequent implementation period. The initial contract period shall be one (1) year, renewable annually based on satisfactory performance and project requirements.

Minimum Qualification Requirements

Interested candidates should possess:

  • Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Sociology, Social Work, Development Studies, Anthropology, Law, or a related field.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in social safeguards or social development.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), with specific knowledge of ESS2 (Labour and Working Conditions) and ESS10 (Stakeholder Engagement and Information Disclosure). Experience in institutional capacity, digital transformation, or statistical projects will be an added advantage.
  • Knowledge of stakeholder engagement and grievance management systems.
  • Familiarity with Labour Management Procedures (LMP) and occupational health and safety requirements applicable to office and government project environments.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, and report-writing skills.
  • Experience working with government institutions and communities.
  • Fluency in English and Amharic.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be obtained from the Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) upon request.

The consultant will be selected using the Selection of Individual Consultants (INDV) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Submission Requirements

Interested candidates shall submit:

  • An Expression of Interest (EOI);
  • Updated Curriculum Vitae (CV); and
  • Supporting documents demonstrating relevant qualifications and experience.

Deadline for Submission: 10 Nov, 2026 at 5:30 PM (Ethiopia Time)

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET DE CONSULTANTS CHARGÉ DE L’ÉLABORATION DE LA STRATÉGIE DE GESTION DES ACTIFS DES PORTS ET DES VOIES NAVIGABLES EN RÉPUBLIQUE DU CONGO

 

1. Les Gouvernements de la République du Congo et de la République Centrafricaine ont signé avec la Banque Mondiale respectivement un accord de prêt et un accord de don pour un montant total de 330 millions USD, dont 90 millions USD pour la République du Congo et 240 millions USD pour la République Centrafricaine, pour la mise en œuvre du Projet Régional d'Amélioration des Corridors de Transport Routier et Fluvial en Afrique centrale (PRACAC). L’Unité de Gestion de Projet (UGP) de la République du Congo a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Elaboration de la stratégie de gestion des actifs des ports et des voies navigables en République du Congo ».

2. L’objectif principal de la mission du consultant est d'appuyer la République du Congo dans la mise en place d'un système efficace et durable de gestion des actifs du transport fluvial, couvrant les infrastructures portuaires, les équipements de navigation, les voies navigables et les moyens flottants, en vue d'assurer leur entretien, leur pérennisation et leur renouvellement programmé dans le cadre du PRACAC. 

3. Le présent avis à manifestation d’intérêt a pour but de solliciter des cabinets de consultants pour faire partie de la liste restreinte en vue de la consultation relative à ladite mission.

4. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet, invite les cabinets éligibles, à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les cabinets peuvent s’associer pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives. Ils doivent fournir les informations ci-après : (i) qualification pour exécuter les services sollicités (références et descriptions concernant l’exécution de missions similaires, brochures…) ; (ii) les capacités techniques du cabinet, les domaines d’intervention ainsi que les années d’expérience du cabinet, les références des clients bénéficiaires des prestations décrites. Les dossiers de manifestation d’intérêt à soumettre ne doivent pas inclure des curriculums vitae, des documents légaux (statuts juridiques, et tous autres documents juridiques), des certificats d’incorporation et/ou une méthodologie de travail.

 

 

5. Les critères pour l'évaluation des Manifestations d’Intérêt sont les suivants : (i) les qualifications générales et expérience du cabinet dans le domaine de la mission, (ii) l'expérience du cabinet dans la réalisation de missions similaires.

6. Il est à noter que les attestations de bonne exécution ou des certificats correspondants signés par les maîtres d’ouvrages faisant mention de la description de missions similaires et des coûts feront foi.

7. L'attention des firmes intéressées est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.15, 3.16 et 3.17 du Règlement de Passation de Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) de la Banque Mondiale, Edition de septembre 2025, relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d'intérêts.

8. Le cabinet/firme sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC), tel que défini dans le Règlement de Passation de Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets (FPI) de la Banque Mondiale, Edition de septembre 2025.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Individual Consultant Selection

Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS)

Reference No.: ET-ESS-574160-CS-INDV

Hiring of Environmental Safeguards Specialist

The Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) intends to recruit an Environmental Safeguards Specialist under the Modernizing Ethiopia's Statistical System Project (MESSP) Preparation Grant, financed by the World Bank.

The Environmental Safeguards Specialist will support environmental risk management and ensure compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable national environmental regulations during MESSP preparation and implementation. The position will focus on environmental screening, monitoring of mitigation measures, occupational health and safety (OHS), e-waste management, environmental reporting, contractor compliance for civil works, and tracking environmental commitments under the project's environmental and social instruments.

Duty Station: ESS Headquarters, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Reporting: The Environmental Safeguards Specialist will report to the Project Manager.

Contract Duration: Full-time assignment. The contract shall commence upon recruitment and cover the project preparation phase and subsequent implementation period. The initial contract period shall be one (1) year, renewable annually based on satisfactory performance and project requirements.

Minimum Qualification Requirements

Interested candidates should possess:

  • Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resource Management, or a related field.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in environmental safeguards, occupational health and safety (OHS) management, or environmental compliance.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing environmental safeguards under World Bank ESF-financed projects is highly desirable; experience with institutional, digital transformation, or ICT-focused projects will be an added advantage.
  • Knowledge of e-waste management standards and OHS requirements applicable to ICT and office environments.
  • Knowledge of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), particularly ESS2 and ESS3, and Ethiopian environmental regulations.
  • Experience in environmental monitoring and reporting.
  • Strong analytical, communication, computer, and reporting skills.
  • Fluency in English and Amharic.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be obtained from the Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) upon request.

The consultant will be selected using the Selection of Individual Consultants (INDV) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Submission Requirements

Interested candidates shall submit:

  • An Expression of Interest (EOI);
  • Updated Curriculum Vitae (CV); and
  • Supporting documents demonstrating relevant qualifications and experience.
